decision: Which domain package should hold the WF-095 rules for collecting quote acceptance by e-signature, countersignature, signer reassignment and identity verification?

state.problem: WF-095 needs pure rules for the acceptance method configuration, signer contacts, countersigners, signer reassignment, the one-hour identity verification window, the 40 MB PDF cap, the signing status machine, quote activity log entries, and quota counting where a three-signature quote counts as one usage.

existing_packages.backend/dsr/quoting_proposals: WF-093. Owns wf093_template, wf093_brand, wf093_document and reads wf086_quote. Its subject is rendering a proposal from a template.
existing_packages.backend/dsr/quote_currency: WF-089. Owns currency records, price lists and pricing runs. Its subject is money.
existing_packages.backend/dsr/identity_verification: WF-078. Owns verified documents, recipients, attempts and sessions. Its subject is a gate before a recipient opens or signs, and it deliberately re-asserts on every attempt.
existing_packages.backend/dsr/mutual_action: WF-124. Owns plan templates, plans, tasks, events and escalations. Its subject is a mutual action plan task graph.

hard_constraints: A feature may not edit any shared file.
Two workflow branches appending to one package initializer collide on the same lines, which is the failure this repository already suffered once.
The domain module imports nothing but the store.

package_choice.instructions: Where should the WF-095 rules live? Weigh the subject each package already owns against the subject this ticket adds, the collision cost of a shared package initializer under four parallel agents, and what a reviewer would have to hold in their head.

criteria.new_package_quote_acceptance: Create backend/dsr/quote_acceptance/ holding vocabulary, rules, inferences and engine, with its own wf095_ collection names. Cost: one more package in the tree. Benefit: acceptance configuration, envelope, signers, signature events and signing status have exactly one owner, and no other branch can collide with it.
criteria.extend_quoting_proposals: Append WF-095 modules to backend/dsr/quoting_proposals. Cost: two tickets edit one package initializer and one vocabulary module, and a reader of quoting_proposals now has to hold template rendering and signature collection. Benefit: the quote itself is already that package's data.
criteria.extend_identity_verification: Append WF-095 modules to backend/dsr/identity_verification. Cost: that package deliberately re-asserts verification on every attempt and owns no document lifecycle, while this ticket's status machine and quota accounting sit outside its subject. Benefit: the one-hour verification window and the identity gate are already vocabulary there.
criteria.extend_mutual_action: Append WF-095 modules to backend/dsr/mutual_action. Cost: a plan task graph is a different subject from a signature envelope, and WF-124 owns its own collections. Benefit: one package instead of two for e-signature-adjacent work.

criteria.true: One option fits the subject, the collision cost and the ownership rule clearly better than the rest
criteria.false: The options are close on this evidence and a human should choose

It touches no shared file.

measurements.design_floor: python tools/check_design_floor.py --feature wf-095-... reported 0 failing, 0 with warnings
measurements.defect_found_and_fixed_over_live_http: A buyer who signed before opening the quote recorded the signature but left the status at pending_signature; opening it afterwards moved the status to viewed_pending_signature, from which nothing could advance it because the buyer had already signed and the countersigner was refused by the order rule. Found by driving the flow out of order over real HTTP, fixed by splitting the status rule into a strict single step (step_status) and a permissive implied-steps rule (advance_status), recorded as DERIVED_SIGNING_IMPLIES_VIEWING, and pinned by four new tests.

declared_unverified: No browser was driven. The page is proven by 35 jsdom tests against its building blocks and by a successful production build; the design-floor checker reads source patterns rather than a render.
No screen reader was run. The ARIA roles and labels are asserted from source and through jsdom queries, but no assistive technology was driven.

Contrast ratios were not measured. The page uses semantic tokens only and no raw hex, and docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md states that foreground and muted-foreground pass 4.5:1 on background and surface, but no computed style was read from a render.
Responsive behaviour was not checked at 375, 768, 1024 or 1440 pixels. The layout uses the documented grid and collapse classes, which the checker does not read.

No verification email was actually sent. The gate is proven end to end because this room mints and holds the token, which the record states: the research names the from-address as a super-admin setting this build does not provision, so the token is returned in the response body and no mail gateway is simulated.

No Dropbox Sign or PandaDoc call was made. The research names both vendors and this build implements the envelope model rather than calling either, because no API key and no cited endpoint contract exists in the sources for either provider in this repository.

The whole-suite run reported 14 failures in backend/tests/test_wf056.py, which this branch does not touch. Removing this branch's files from the worktree reproduced exactly the same failures, so they are pre-existing on this checkout and not caused by this change. They were not fixed because the file belongs to another workflow.

The whole-suite and coverage figures were measured on a machine running four agents at once, so the wall-clock figure understates what a clean runner would show. The pass and fail counts are not affected by contention.

The gate is proven end to end because this room mints and holds the token, which the record states: the research names the from-address as a super-admin setting this build does not provision, so the token is returned in the response body and no mail gateway is simulated.

No Dropbox Sign or PandaDoc call was made. The research names both vendors and this build implements the envelope model rather than calling either, because no API key and no cited endpoint contract exists in the sources for either provider in this repository.

The whole-suite run reported 14 failures in backend/tests/test_wf056.py, which this branch does not touch. Removing this branch's files from the worktree reproduced exactly the same failures, so they are pre-existing on this checkout and not caused by this change. They were not fixed because the file belongs to another workflow.

The whole-suite and coverage figures were measured on a machine running four agents at once, so the wall-clock figure understates what a clean runner would show. The pass and fail counts are not affected by contention.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
